writing.overall_comment: A well-organized and readable testing skill with clear principles and numeric targets, but its heavy reliance on abstract placeholders and deferral of real examples to a reference file keeps it from being fully concrete or executable on its own.

dimensions.name: Semantic accuracy
dimensions.comment: The name and description accurately reflect the skill's coverage of unit/integration testing, TDD/BDD, mocking, and coverage guidance, though the promised 'multiple languages' and 'test automation' content is only referenced, not delivered in-doc.

dimensions.name: Examples & edge cases
dimensions.comment: Examples are largely language-agnostic placeholders (e.g., [Prepare test objects]) rather than concrete runnable cases, and while failure paths like null inputs and exceptions are listed, no worked failure-path examples are shown.

dimensions.name: Actionability
dimensions.comment: The Red-Green-Refactor cycle, concrete coverage targets, and mock-vs-don't-mock rules are explicit and usable, but many sections are opinionated checklists without rationale and the templates require the reader to fill in blanks themselves.

suggestions: Replace placeholder examples such as [Prepare test objects] with concrete, runnable, language-specific test snippets in the Examples & edge cases section.
Add a brief rationale for each rule in the opinionated checklist sections to explain why the practice matters.
Turn fill-in-the-blank templates into completed worked examples or annotate each blank with sample values so readers can apply them without guessing.
